Traditional Tibetan Butter Tea

Served at: Losar (Tibetan New Year)

Serves 4Prep 10 minCook 15 min

Butter tea, or Po Cha, is a traditional Tibetan beverage made from tea leaves, yak butter, salt, and water. It is especially popular during Losar, the Tibetan New Year, as it symbolizes warmth, hospitality, and sustenance in the cold Himalayan climate.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (950 ml) water
  • 2 tablespoons loose black tea leaves (preferably Tibetan or strong black tea)
  • 4 tablespoons unsalted butter (preferably yak butter, or substitute with unsalted cow butter)
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • Optional: 1/4 cup (60 ml) milk or cream

Method

  1. Bring the water to a boil in a saucepan.
  2. Add the black tea leaves to the boiling water and simmer for 10 minutes to make a strong brew.
  3. Strain the tea leaves out and pour the hot tea into a traditional churn or a blender.
  4. Add the butter and salt to the hot tea.
  5. Churn or blend the mixture vigorously for 3-5 minutes until the butter is fully melted and the tea becomes frothy and well mixed.
  6. If desired, stir in milk or cream for a richer taste.
  7. Serve the butter tea hot in small bowls or cups.

Tips

  • Use a traditional Tibetan butter tea churn if available for authentic texture.
  • Adjust the amount of salt and butter to taste; butter tea is traditionally quite salty and rich.
  • For a vegan alternative, use plant-based butter and omit milk or cream.
